why: `lifecycle::trampolines::on_cleanup::<T>` -- the monomorphized `extern "C"` shim that recovers `&mut T` from the FFI context pointer and calls `LifecycleCallbacks::on_cleanup`. One per `T`, emitted by rustc, so a safe trait can be registered through a C function-pointer slot with no allocation. Public because `Executor::register_lifecycle_node` names them, not because a user calls them. **rclrs 0.5.1 has no lifecycle support whatsoever** -- the whole stage reports zero theirs-only rows in the Rust lane -- so every item here is an extension by definition. The RTOS scenario is REP-2002 itself: a device that owns hardware needs a supervisor-driven `configure`/`activate`/`deactivate` protocol so an actuator can be brought up and parked without restarting the image, and `ros2 lifecycle set` is how the rest of the graph asks for it. We implement the state machine once in `nros_core::lifecycle` and surface it in all three languages.
